clinician.trajectory_summary: A 39-year-old woman presented with an abdominal mass, weight loss, and abnormal bleeding. Gynecological transabdominal ultrasonography revealed an adnexal solid mass, leading to suspicion of ovarian carcinoma. Laparotomy revealed a large, ruptured right adnexal mass with cystic and solid parts, adhesions, and ascitic fluid. Histopathological examination confirmed the diagnosis of right ovarian malignant Brenner tumors, which had infiltrated the corpus uteri, invaded the lymph vasculature, and metastasized to 2 right pelvic lymph nodes, 1 left pelvic lymph node, rectum, prevesical space, and Douglas pouch.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with an abdominal mass, weight loss, and a 2-year history of bleeding outside of her menstrual cycle.
Gynecological transabdominal ultrasonography (USG) revealed an adnexal solid mass measuring 11.86×12.50×11.24 cm.

Laparotomy revealed a 25×20×15 cm grayish cystic mass with solid parts and an irregular surface originating from the right adnexa that adhered to the omentum and peritoneum, with rupture on the posterior surface and ascitic fluid.
Histopathological examination revealed the diagnosis of right ovarian malignant Brenner tumors.
The tumor infiltrated the corpus uteri, invaded the lymph vasculature, and metastasized to 2 right pelvic lymph nodes, 1 left pelvic lymph node, rectum, prevesical space, and Douglas pouch.
